title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a profinite completion of the 'isotopic category' of anabelian oriented surfaces. On the previous page (16), objects are surfaces and Aut are mapping class groups; the goal is a target on which Gal(Qbar/Q) can act. That page works with a category C already carrying topologies. It shows that, for u: X→Y and v: Y→Z, the map Aut(Y)→Hom(X,Z), φ ↦ vφu, is continuous, given hypothesis (16)(*). Write G_u = {(ψ,φ) ∈ Aut(X)×Aut(Y) | φu = uψ} for the stabiliser of u. Hypothesis (*) says that the image H_u of G_u in Aut(Y) has finite index; equivalently, since H_u is closed, it is open.

This page abstracts the construction. Let C_0 be a bare category, with no topology, satisfying the purely algebraic condition (*): for every arrow u: X→Y, pr_2(G_u) has finite index in Aut(Y). Grothendieck claims there is a functor C_0 → Ĉ_0 into an 'essentially profinite' category. The bracket defines this notion, and the margin note 'devrait suffire' says the definition should suffice:
- each Hom(X,Y) is locally compact;
- composition is continuous;
- Aut(X), topologised as {(u,v) | uv = id, vu = id} ⊂ Hom(X,X)×Hom(X,X), is a profinite group;
- the Aut(X)×Aut(Y)^op-orbits in Hom(X,Y) are open.

The 'profinite envelope' Ĉ_0 has the same objects as C_0, and (17) defines
Hom_{Ĉ_0}(X,Y) = Hom_{C_0}(X,Y) ×^{Aut(X)×Aut(Y)^op} (Âut(X)×Âut(Y)).
In other words, each orbit G/G_u (G = Aut X × Aut Y) is replaced by its profinite completion Ĝ/closure(G_u). The result is a disjoint sum of compact (profinite) homogeneous spaces, hence locally compact.

Grothendieck then asserts that this is isomorphic to the completion using only Aut(X): Hom_{C_0}(X,Y)^∧ relative to Aut(X) → Âut(X). The reason is that each G-orbit is a finite union of Aut(X)-orbits, since Aut(X)\G/G_u ≅ Aut(Y)/H_u is finite by (*).

Composition in Ĉ_0 is determined uniquely by two requirements: continuity, and extending the composition of C_0 (density). Its existence rests on the continuity lemma of the previous page. The page breaks off at 'Par construction, tout Ĉ_0-morphisme…'.

The next page applies this to the isotopic category of anabelian surfaces. There the Hom^∧ are locally compact, countable at infinity, totally disconnected and metrisable. It then restricts to surfaces carrying a complex algebraic structure, in order to describe these morphisms algebro-geometrically and so get a Galois action. In short, this page is the general categorical engine behind the profinite Teichmüller tower in its non-groupoid, 'category with embeddings' form.
errors: The isomorphism in (17) between completing with respect to Aut(X)×Aut(Y)^op and with respect to Aut(X) alone is not automatic. The profinite topology that the G-set G/G_u (G = Aut X × Aut Y) induces on an Aut(X)-orbit Aut(X)/S_X, with S_X = {ψ | uψ = u}, could be coarser than that orbit's own profinite topology. One needs finite-index subgroups M ⊇ S_X of Aut(X) that are normalised by pr_1(G_u). This holds, for example, if Aut(X) is finitely generated: intersect all subgroups of index ≤ n, then take L = M'·G_u, which has finite index because A·G_u has finite index by (*). The hypothesis is satisfied for mapping class groups but is not stated.

Existence and associativity of the extended composition are asserted ('de façon unique, d'ailleurs') rather than proved. Existence relies on the continuity argument of the previous page, which uses (*) only for the middle object Y; a full check of joint continuity of composition, in both variables, is not written out.

The definition of 'essentially profinite' does not require the canonical functor C_0 → Ĉ_0 to be faithful. That would need residual finiteness of the orbits (G_u closed in the profinite topology), which is not discussed here; it is harmless for the construction itself.

ideas.what: Profinite envelope of an arbitrary (non-groupoid) category: keep the objects and replace each Hom-set, viewed as an Aut(X)×Aut(Y)^op-set, by its profinite completion induced to Âut(X)×Âut(Y). Composition is extended by continuity.
ideas.modern_name: profinite completion of a category / of the Teichmüller tower (non-groupoid version); induced profinite G-sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Profinite Teichmüller groupoid: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), then Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Boggi. Profinite completion of categories and operads: e.g. Horel (2017) and others.
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses the profinite completion of the Teichmüller tower/groupoid, but not, as far as I know, this general categorical construction with condition (*).

ideas.what: Purely algebraic finiteness condition (*): the image in Aut(Y) of the stabiliser of every arrow u: X→Y has finite index. This guarantees continuity of composition after completion.
ideas.modern_name: finite-index stabiliser condition; analogous to 'commensurator/finite orbit' conditions for completing actions
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution known to me

ideas.what: Axiomatisation of an 'essentially profinite category': locally compact Hom spaces, continuous composition, profinite Aut groups with the topology induced via pairs (u,v) with uv = vu = id, open Aut×Aut-orbits.
ideas.modern_name: category enriched in locally profinite spaces with profinite automorphism groups (cf. profinite groupoids, Galois categories)

ideas.what: Reduction of the two-sided completion to a one-sided one (completion with respect to Aut(X) only), using finiteness of Aut(X)\G/G_u ≅ Aut(Y)/H_u.
ideas.modern_name: induction/restriction of profinite G-sets along a finite double-coset decomposition

missed.claim: A general theorem: any category satisfying the algebraic condition (*) admits a canonical 'profinite envelope' Ĉ_0 with continuous composition, uniquely determined. This is a universal completion for categories with non-invertible morphisms, not just groupoids. Grothendieck states it, flags 'devrait suffire' and leaves the proof. Published profinite Teichmüller theory works mostly with groupoids or operads, not with this Hom-wise completion under a finite-index stabiliser hypothesis.
missed.quote: Je dis qu'on peut alors trouver une solution au pb d'envoyer C_0, par un foncteur, dans une catégorie C "essentiellement profinie" … en prenant comme "enveloppe profinie" Ĉ_0 …
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean criterion for profinitely completing categories of surfaces with embeddings (rather than just the mapping-class groupoid). It could be compared with modern profinite completions of operads, ∞-categories and Teichmüller towers (Horel, Boavida–Horel–Robertson, Boggi), on which the absolute Galois group or GT should act.

missed.claim: Condition (*) as the precise hypothesis making Galois/GT actions extend from mapping class groups to embedding morphisms. This links completion of categories of surfaces with the non-groupoid 'isotopic category' that Grothendieck uses before restricting to complex algebraic curves on the next page.
missed.quote: (16) (*) … H_u … est un sous-groupe d'indice fini de Aut(Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In modern GT literature, morphisms between surfaces of different types are handled through operads or groupoids of base points. A categorical framework with this explicit finiteness condition might simplify statements about profinite subsurface/embedding maps.

deep.surprise_reason: The overall goal, a profinite Teichmüller tower with a Galois action, is well known from the Esquisse. The explicit general construction is a detail not in the published record as far as I know: a profinite envelope of an arbitrary category under the algebraic finite-index stabiliser condition (*), with an axiomatised 'essentially profinite category'. It is natural, however, and close in spirit to later profinite completions of operads and groupoids.
transcription_corrections: Marginal addition near (17) should read 'avec la top. d'espaces sommes d'espaces compacts …' ('sommes', not 'souvent'), matching the next page's 'espaces sommes top. d'espaces compacts'.
In (17) the exponent '0' on Aut(Y) is 'o' (opposite group): Aut(X)×Aut(Y)^o; the completion is relative to Âut(X)×Âut(Y).
The bracketed insertion reads roughly 'avec compositions continues' (continuity of composition), placed under 'les Hom(X,Y) sont des espaces loc. compacts'.
Left margin 'devrait suffire' refers to the bracketed definition of 'essentiellement profinie'.
'Hom_C(X,Y)' in the line 'dans Hom_C(X,Y) sont ouvertes' — subscript C confirmed.
'dans une catégorie C' — the letter C is written above 'catégorie'.
